cases.reason: The diagrams are identical, but the format's operand data-name-1 admits more in 2002. 2002 SR4 says only that data-name-1 'may be qualified', and by 2002 5.1.3 a data-name in a general format is a user-defined word 'including qualification and subscription if needed'; 2023 SR4 says data-name-1 'shall not be subject to any OCCURS clauses' (2014 E.2 item 25 records this restriction as added after 2002). So START F KEY >= RKT(1), where RKT(1) is a table element meeting 2002 SR6b (leftmost position of the prime key, same class, shorter), is legal 2002 and illegal 2023; the 2023 row's evidence says nothing about it. Probe start_subkey.cob: at --std 2002 it compiles and positions correctly (GOT BB02 second); at --std 2023 it is refused (COBOL0862, §2023:14.9.41.3 SR4). compiler-at-2002: correct. needs: a 2002 witness for a subscripted START KEY data-name-1 (candidate start_subkey.cob).

The syntax rules match (2002 SR8 = 2023 SR9 on omitting DELIMITED); 2023's added SR3 (zero-length literal) and SR11 (variable-length group) name 2023-only constructs. Operands that are CD record items qualified by cd-name (2002 8.4.1.1 file-cd-report-qualifier) are a generic identifier reach, not this format's: probe str_cd.cob runs correctly at --std 2002 (Q [ABCDEF] P 07).

TERMINATE { report-name-1 } ... identical; no operand difference.
UNLOCK format identical. 2023 SR2 (APPLY COMMIT) restricts a 2023-only clause and reaches no 2002 program.

UNSTRING format identical; 2002 SR1 to SR9 equal 2023's; 2023 SR10 (variable-length group, a 2023-only construct per §2023:8.5.1.12) reaches no 2002 program. CD-record operands: probe str_cd.cob UNSTRING R-Q IN CIN runs correctly at --std 2002.

USE formats 1 to 4 identical except class-name-1 / object-class-name-1 (same SR16). Format 3 exception-name operand: every EC- name in the 2002 text also occurs in the 2023 text (mechanical diff, ec02.txt vs ec23.txt in the probe folder; the one leftover is a line-break artefact of EC-PROGRAM-ARG-OMITTED). No 2002 Annex A USE form.
PROGRAM-ID formats identical, including the choice indicators; 2023 SR1 adds only the zero-length-literal exclusion (no zero-length literals exist in 2002). SR2 to SR6 identical.

Two differences. (1) communication-reach: the 2002 communication section format admits constant-entry after a communication description entry (A.1.1), so 13.9.1 governs constant entries in the COMMUNICATION SECTION, which 2023 does not have. Probe const_cd.cob at --std 2002: constants with literal, arithmetic expression, IS GLOBAL, BYTE-LENGTH OF and LENGTH OF a CD record item compile and print 7, 5, 12, 87 (correct); refused at 2023 (COBOL0902). (2) removed-form, a compiler DEFECT: 2002 SR3 says only that data-name-1 and data-name-2 'may be qualified' (with 5.1.3 subscripting allowed if needed); 2023 SR3 requires 'All subscripts ... shall be literals' (added in 2014). Probe const_sub.cob: LENGTH OF T(I) and BYTE-LENGTH OF T(I + 1) are refused at --std 2002 with COBOL1547 citing §2023:13.10.3 SR3, a 2023 rule applied to legal 2002 source (same family as PB5602). needs: a 2002 witness for constant entries in the communication section (candidate const_cd.cob) and a fix plus witness for non-literal subscripts (const_sub.cob).
